constraints.evidence: Slide 16: Option A peak need $1.9M (11% of the $18M cap); slide 18 worst case (32% ACoS, 25% duty) low point $3.9M. Slide 9: Option B cumulative cash -$20.8M by 2030, passing the cap in 2029. The cap screens out B, not A.
Slides 16-18 and the governing thought: A pays back in 2030 only below 28.6% average ACoS. End-2030 cash is +$2.4M at 25%, +$0.38M at 28%, -$2.32M at 32%. B never pays back (slide 9).

Slide 10: group margin with B is 4.5%, 6.6%, 7.5%, 8.2% in 2027-30 against the 8% floor. The 2027 US loss of $8.7M takes 56% of the $15.4M ex-US profit. A stays at 9.5% or more even in the launch year. The check is year by year.

Slide 8 footnote: bandwidth allows one launch in 2027, so the options are mutually exclusive. J is carried as a full option with a cash break-even against A (25.9% ACoS), a $7M revenue comparison, and a fallback role (slide 19).

Slide 15: neither route reaches $40M. A reaches $26.4M (66%) and B $37.6M (94%) but only at a cash cost the board ruled out. It says to read 'on the way to $40M' as about $26M in 2030, with retail next. $40M by Amazon alone would need 1.5x the plan volume.

Slide 11: 4.0 removal line. Onsoo's 9% awareness sits in the lowest band (median 2.6), so Onsoo would likely be removed at the first review. The CEO's 15% gate sits in the 10-20% band (3.5), still under 4.0. Gate 4 therefore requires awareness above 20% (median 4.6).

Slide 14: per-unit build with price 24, referral 3.6, FBA 5.1, product 3.5, freight and duty 1.075, advertising 6, giving $4.725 contribution at 25% ACoS (19.7% of price). Contribution is $3.05 at 32%. Retail uses $14 wholesale and Table 4 costs. Payback is built on contribution, not revenue.

Slide 16: $9.2M of fixed and setup costs in A's 2030 cash. Slide 9: $40.8M of fixed and one-time costs for B. Slide 22 itemises the retail cost lines ($6.0M marketing, $1.5M field team, $0.5M fee, $1,100 per door).

Inventory is deducted in the headline cash builds: $1.7M at end-2030 for A (slide 16), $2.6M for B (slide 9), and $0.2M for the 2029 retail layer (slide 22). The 28.6% break-even (slide 17) also includes inventory in the $10.9M.

Slide 17: the plan assumes 25% 'because ACoS falls as the brand matures'; 'Agency data shows the opposite at scale... median 32% (26%-38%)'. Slide 18 gives end-2030 cash at each ACoS from 25% to 38%. Governing thought: pays back only below 28.6%.

Slide 17: a duty rise to 25% lowers the break-even to about 26.9%. Slide 18: -$3.4M at 32% ACoS and 25% duty. Slide 14: +$0.35 per unit. Gate 1 uses 26.9% if the duty rises, and the CFO re-runs the model after the tariff ruling.

Gate 2: US-compliant English labels on every unit from launch (6% of reviews cite Korean-only text). Compliance is in the $2.1M a year and $0.8M setup in the $9.2M. Next steps: MoCRA and labels in Q2 2027.

Slides 6 and 18 and gate 3 cite 29% vs 31% vs 48% and say 'loyalty is not yet proven'. The volume ramp is still the planning team's. The document does not show how repeat changes volumes or cash, or say the ramp cannot rely on Korean repeat or on continued pilot growth.

alternatives.evidence: Option B is modelled on the board's limits (slides 8-11). It breaks the cap (-$20.8M, -$26.4M at 2.6 units per door), has no payback, and takes 2027 group margin to 4.5%. The 4.5 units per door is shown to be the above-20% band, and the 1.3x halo is challenged (0.71 correlation). Mooncrest (-$21M) is the precedent (slide 12).

A smaller regional retail test is named. 'Not costed in the briefing pack'; the next step is to cost it in H2 2028 (slides 22 and 24). It is not tested, and only a national retail layer from 2029 is costed (-$11.9M).

Slides 8 and 19: J meets every limit but builds $7M against $26.4M in 2030. Japan wins on cash above 25.9% ACoS, and the document states the cash assumption (cash taken equal to operating result). It is adopted as the fallback if gate 1 fails. The mid-2027 tariff and the 1.5% Japan growth are covered. Japan's own peak cash and payback year are not stated.

No leaner Amazon-led variant is considered (smaller team, slower brand spend). Fixed costs of $2.1M a year are taken as given. The document never quantifies how a fixed-cost cut would move the 28.6% break-even.

sensitivities.evidence: Slide 18: end-2030 cash at 25% (+2.40), 26%, 28% (+0.38), 30%, 32% (-2.32), 35% and 38% (-6.37), with $0.67M per ACoS point. Break-even is 28.6%, falling to 26.9% at 25% duty. 32% ACoS plus 25% duty gives -$3.4M, with a low point of $3.9M (22% of the cap). Gate 1 states the response if missed.

Slide 11: plan 4.5, above 20% awareness 4.6, 10-20% 3.5, below 10% 2.6, and removal at 4.0. B's cash is -$26.4M at 2.6. Covering $7.5M a year would take about 32 units per door. Gate 4 sets the awareness required (above 20%), not the CEO's 15%.

Slide 6 notes June's run rate is 168,000 a year, 56% of A's 2027 plan, with three of seven SKUs. Slide 15: $40M needs 1.5x plan volume. There is no volume shortfall or cushion test for A's payback and no volume or repeat trigger for scaling, holding or stopping. Gate 3 covers repeat only. The Saebom vs Gaon Lab/Yeoreum spread is shown on slide 12 but not tied to the ramp.

omissions: No volume cushion or volume-based scale/hold/stop trigger. The payback has little room, yet the plan never states how far Amazon volume can fall short of the ramp (300k to 1.1M units) before payback fails. The four gates cover ACoS, labels, repeat and awareness only.

Gate 1 is defined as a 2027-30 sales-weighted average ACoS (28.6%), but it is reviewed at end-2027. No year-one ACoS value or leading indicator is given for the go/no-go. Switching to Japan in 2028 is not costed, even though Japan's modelled ramp starts in 2027.
The worst-case cash envelope is requested without a figure in the recommendation or next steps. The $3.9M appears only in a slide 18 footnote.
No lean Amazon-led option (fixed-cost cuts) and no costed staged retail test. The regional test is deferred to H2 2028, after the gate 4 decision and with no cost basis.
unsupported_assumptions: "On the planning team's inputs, Amazon-led needs at most $1.9M and pays back in 2030" (slide 16): the headline cash path uses a 25% ACoS 'because ACoS falls as the brand matures', which is below the pilot (28%) and the agency median (32%). The document flags this, but gives no evidence for 25%.

Option A volumes of 300,000 rising to 1.1M units, 'the planning team's', with four extra SKUs and repeat below benchmark. The document gives no demand build from the pilot or channel economics beyond comparing 2027 to the June run rate.
"the hero product's economics apply to all SKUs" (slide 14): the $4.73 contribution is applied to the seven-SKU plan. The document states this but gives no basis.

Option B at the retailer's 4.5 units per door is used for the headline $20.8M, and the 2029 retail layer is costed with no Amazon halo. This is stated, but the Amazon impact of retail is not tested either way.
